title: A mobile-first public health education website for Illinois…
brief: A mobile-first public health education website for Illinois Medicaid patients and their families. Patients reach it by scanning a QR code on a printed flyer. It must answer, fast, on a phone: Is this change about me? What do I do now? Who do I call? Where can I get care if I lose coverage? Content: key dates, work requirements, exemptions, how to keep coverage, non-citizen rules, what to do if you lose Medicaid, phone numbers, and a list of free and low-cost clinics in Cook County. Plain language at roughly a 6th-grade reading level, WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 text contrast, visible focus, 44px targets), friendly and calm, not corporate. Home page is a hub: a short 'Does this apply to you?' section, then big tappable cards to each topic, then 'Who to call'. Built as plain HTML/CSS/JS. Each direction is a sketch of the home page on a phone-width and desktop-width layout.

directions.spec:
### Forest Green (matches the printed flyer)  `(id: forest-green-matches-the-printed-flyer)`

Use the flyer's own palette so patients recognize it from the poster: forest green #2f5f28 as the primary color, mint #eaf3e7 for panels and callouts, white page background, near-black text. Numbered steps in solid green circles with white numerals. Soft rounded cards (12-16px radius). Clean humanist sans-serif. Calm, institutional but warm. This direction must keep that palette; vary layout and type only within it.

directions.spec:
### Civic Clear (public-service, high contrast)  `(id: civic-clear-public-service-high-contrast)`

A plain-spoken public-service look in the spirit of government design systems: deep navy primary, a warm gold accent used sparingly for highlights and the 'Who to call' strip, white background, black text. Large type (18px body on mobile), strong left-aligned headings, thick top borders on cards instead of shadows, chunky full-width buttons, almost no decoration. Feels official, fast and trustworthy.

### Warm Clinic (soft, friendly)  `(id: warm-clinic-soft-friendly)`

Warm and reassuring like a good community clinic: cream page background, teal primary, coral accent for key actions, soft pill-shaped buttons and tags, generous spacing, a friendly rounded humanist sans. Topic cards use a small simple icon and a one-line 'this is for you if...' hint. Feels like a person helping you, not a form.
